newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu and King Hussein to meet in Red Sea port.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu and King Hussein to meet in Red Sea port.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Jordan on Wednesday for talks with King Hussein on the crisis in the Middle East peace process, a palace official said on Sunday.
The two leaders are expected to meet in Jordan's southern Red Sea port of Aqaba, the official said.

Their planned talks come amid a flurry of regional meetings aimed at containing a Palestinian-Israeli crisis after a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem last month and Israel's closure of Palestinian territories.

Washington's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was in Israel on Sunday for talks with Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat. Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy has held talks in Jordan and Egypt, and Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan flew to Jerusalem and Alexandria last week.

In the wake of the Jerusalem bombings, which killed 13 people as well as the bombers, Netanyahu insisted Arafat clamp down on militants as a prerequisite for resuming talks on expanding Palestinian self-rule.
Arafat has called the Israeli security clampdown "state terrorism" against the Palestinians.
